node-1.label: Patient had a painless neck lump first noticed 6 years ago that recently grew rapidly

node-2.label: 26-year-old male had a painless neck lump first noticed 6 years ago that had recently grown rapidly; he experienced agitation, irritability, excessive sweating, and discomfort while swallowing; he had previously been diagnosed with nodular goiter at other hospitals and intermittently took Euthyrox for several years; he reported childhood hearing impairment and language learning difficulties, with clinical examination indicating normal mental and physical development

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed a visible grade III goiter, with an enlarged, tough thyroid without palpable nodules and a clear boundary

node-4.label: Laboratory tests showed free thyroxine 9.99 pmol/l (normal 11.5–23.5), free triiodothyronine 6.07 pmol/l (normal 3.5–6.5), and thyroid stimulating hormone 2.401 μlU/ml (normal 0.3–5.0); thyrotrophin receptor, thyroglobulin, thyroperoxidase antibodies, carcinoembryonic antigen, thyroglobulin, and calcitonin levels were within normal ranges

node-5.label: Chest X-ray showed tracheal narrowing at the superior thoracic aperture; thyroid ultrasound revealed multiple hypoechoic signals in each lobe and isthmus of the thyroid and cervical lymph node enlargement; cervical computed tomography showed diffuse enlargement of each lobe and thickening of the thyroid isthmus, with numerous oval low- and slightly high-density nodules; electrical capacitance tomography results were consistent with signs of a nodular goiter

attrs.why: Both expert pathologist and laboratory physician analyses favor malignant thyroid tumor at 0.65, based on 6-year painless lump with recent rapid growth, firm grade III goiter, cervical lymphadenopathy, tracheal narrowing, and multinodular hypoechoic thyroid; normal calcitonin and antibodies refute medullary and autoimmune thyroiditis. FNA, molecular testing, and surgical pathology remain pending, so malignancy remains unconfirmed and confidence remains 0.65.

Benign nodular goiter remains a close alternative at 0.60 because of the long-standing nodular goiter, multiple nodules, ECT signs, and tracheal compression, although rapid growth and cervical lymphadenopathy are atypical. Normal thyroid antibodies, euthyroid/low free thyroxine, and nodular imaging refute autoimmune thyroiditis; laboratory physician analysis also notes normal antibodies refute autoimmune thyroiditis, and hypoechoic changes are nonspecific. Confidence remains 0.15.
Childhood hearing impairment/language difficulty and goiter suggest hereditary syndrome (e.g., Pendred); rapid growth/lymphadenopathy not typical.
